To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Thursday launch handover for Inês

DRAFT — for me to read on the train before sharing.

Inês,

I’m sorry to leave you with this, especially with a correction to sort out two days before the launch. My father is ill, I am with my family. I don’t yet know how long I’ll be away. You can call me, but after 09:00 tomorrow, Tuesday, I might not pick up. Please don’t make progress depend on reaching me.

I trust you completely with Thursday. You know this paper as well as I do, and you ran the annex B sensitivity work yourself. You don’t need to try to deliver my presentation in my voice. Make it yours, cut what you need to, and use your own judgement in the room.

The most urgent thing is the wrong revenue number already in the embargoed release. Everything else comes after getting that correction moving.

1. First: get the correction to Hanna and fix the deck

The correct estimate for 2030 LDC-relevant revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. Figure 3 and the summary had picked up the old run, which did not apply the free allocation phase-out. The paper’s conclusion does not change, but the headline number does. We need to be clear about both, not minimise the correction.

PDF v7 in the launch folder is corrected on pages 3, 14 and 15. Use that as the reference version.

Still to fix:
- Deck v4, slides 6 and 9. Slide 9 contains the revenue chart.
- The embargoed press release Hanna sent on Friday to 34 Brussels contacts.

Please contact Hanna first and ask her to arrange a corrected release and an explicit correction to everyone who received the original. The embargo lifts at 10:00 CET on Thursday 26 November; we should get the replacement to people well before then, not wait for launch morning. Ask her to make it unmistakable which version supersedes Friday’s release and to confirm when the correction has gone out.

Geert knows I am away. If Hanna needs a senior name to sign off the corrected release, he can do it. There is no need to wait for me.

Suggested correction wording, for you and Hanna to adapt:

“The 2030 estimate for LDC-relevant CBAM revenue is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion as stated in the earlier release. The earlier figure came from a run that did not apply the free allocation phase-out. The corrected estimate is in PDF v7. The paper’s conclusion is unchanged.”

This is my mistake, not yours. If anyone asks who was responsible, please say so plainly: “That was Marieke’s error.” You do not need to take responsibility for it because you are presenting the corrected work.

Once the release correction is underway, update slides 6 and 9 and check the speaker notes, chart labels and any other mentions of 2.1 in the launch materials. Save a clearly labelled corrected deck so nobody picks up v4 by accident. Please ask Hanna to check that anything she distributes or publishes uses PDF v7 and the corrected number. A second pair of eyes on the final release and slides would be useful.

2. Tuesday: settle the revised programme with Tomás

The run of show in the folder is out of date. Tomás emailed today: Lindqvist has a vote and must leave at 13:30. She wants the presentation reduced to 15 minutes, the panel to start at 12:50, and time to take at least two questions herself before leaving.

Please tell Tomás you are replacing me for both the presentation and the panel, and agree the revised running order with him. The working outline is:

- 12:00: guests at the security entrance; Tomás collects badges. Light lunch is also listed from 12:00 outside the room.
- 12:30–12:35: Lindqvist’s welcome.
- 12:35–12:50: your presentation.
- 12:50: panel starts.
- Before 13:30: space for Lindqvist to take at least two questions.
- 13:30: Lindqvist leaves.
- 14:00: close, unless her office confirms a change.

Two things need an actual answer from the office: when those first audience questions will happen, and who moderates after 13:30. The old plan has Q&A at 13:40 and Lindqvist moderating throughout, so it cannot simply stay as written. Ask Tomás to circulate the agreed version to the speakers.

Final names from our side must reach Tomás by Wednesday 25 November at 12:00 latest. Security will not admit people whose names are missing. Make sure your name is on the final list, along with anyone coming to support you. The venue remains the European Parliament, Altiero Spinelli building, in the room booked by Lindqvist’s office.

3. Tuesday/Wednesday: prepare your 15 minutes and the panel

The deck is 14 slides, but please don’t feel obliged to use all of them. Once the numbers are corrected, cut it to a comfortable 15 minutes and rehearse that version. My notes are still in the deck; they are there to help, not to dictate how you speak.

Kessler has already said he will raise the 80% pass-through assumption and resource shuffling. Don’t let him turn the whole launch into an argument about one central-case assumption. Answer him directly, acknowledge the limits, then bring the discussion back to the paper’s findings and the LDC question.

On pass-through, the honest answer is:

“80% is our central case. Annex B also tests 60% and 40%. The result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%, so we are not claiming the finding is equally strong under every assumption.”

You know those runs better than anyone in the room. There’s no need to sound defensive or to concede more than the analysis says.

On resource shuffling: we agree it is a risk, discuss it in section 5.2, and recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. Acknowledge that rather than treating it as an objection we overlooked.

Abena is joining remotely from the Accra Trade Policy Centre. The link is in the calendar invitation, and your deck note says she tested it successfully. Please let her know you are taking over and that the timing has changed, and arrange a quick sound/link check with the room team before the event. She was strong on the LDC side in our call; invite her perspective, but don’t assume she will answer for us or back every point.

And remember Lisbon. When the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel without making it look like a rescue. You are better live than you think. A difficult question or a broken slide does not change that.

4. Wednesday: press calls and final checks

Hanna promised two journalists a call on Wednesday afternoon: one from a trade newsletter and one from a Belgian daily. The calendar has 14:00 and 15:00 on Wednesday 25 November, 20 minutes each by phone, but these are marked “Hanna to confirm”.

Ask Hanna to confirm the times and contacts and tell them you are covering for me. If those slots collide with essential preparation, ask her to rearrange them rather than trying to do everything at once. Before either call, make sure the journalist has the corrected release and PDF v7. Use the same clear explanation of the correction in both calls.

By Wednesday evening, aim to have:
- Hanna’s confirmation that the corrected release has reached the original recipients.
- The corrected deck checked against PDF v7.
- Your presentation timed to 15 minutes.
- Badges confirmed following the noon deadline.
- The revised programme agreed, including questions before 13:30 and moderation afterwards.
- Abena briefed on the changes and a room/link check arranged.

5. Thursday and afterwards

Have the corrected deck and PDF v7 saved locally as well as on the drive. Coordinate arrival with Tomás so there is time to test the presentation and remote connection before the audience arrives.

Please arrange someone to take two usable event photos and record attendance numbers. Lucy Tran at Halvorsen is attending with a colleague and needs those for the grant report, ideally by 4 December. You shouldn’t have to remember photography while presenting; ask someone supporting the event to own it.

Afterwards, put the final materials, attendance count and photos in the launch folder, and arrange the follow-up to Lucy by 4 December. Anything substantive that needs a later answer can be noted and followed up; you don’t have to improvise a definitive answer to every question in the room.

If anyone asks about my absence, the only personal wording I want shared is: “My father is ill, I am with my family.” No further details, please.

I am sorry about the timing, the extra work, and especially leaving you to handle a mistake that is mine. Thank you for taking this on. I trust your judgement completely, including when you decide to do something differently from how I would have done it.

Marieke

reasons: The opening says the correction comes 'two days before the launch', but the piece is written on Monday 23 Nov and the launch is Thursday 26 Nov, which is three days.
